one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests only that clamp is exported and returns x limited to lo..hi; every case, including the boundaries and lo===hi, follows from those words. Check 2 tests only that calls with lo>hi throw a RangeError. Check 3 requires an entry for each exported function that "names it and describes what it does", which is a fair reading of "documents". The note "(expect at least add, subtract, multiply, clamp)" is a hint about what the command will print, not an extra test. Check 4 is just "no failing tests". The stricter items are all under "Advisory": the grep screen, placement under "## API", mentioning RangeError in the README, exit status 0, added clamp tests and the error message wording. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond its expect line.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the five tracked files and the test script ("node --test"). `npm test` will run, and node --test finds test/math.test.js. Every `node -e` command loads ./math.js, which exists, and the JavaScript in each one is valid: the destructuring loops, try/catch with instanceof RangeError, and Object.keys(...).filter(...).join('\n') all parse. The shell quoting works too. Each script sits in double quotes and uses only single quotes inside. There is no `$` or backtick. The `!==` in Check 1 is not history-expanded, because bash leaves a `!` followed by `=` alone. The `'\n'` passes through to JavaScript unchanged. The advisory `grep -nE '^#+ .*(add|subtract|multiply|clamp)\(' README.md` is a valid extended regex with a literal paren, run on an existing file. The builder's commit and PR steps name no missing tools.

catches-traps.why: I checked each must_catch item against the briefs. Item 1: builder step 3 says "subtract is exported but currently NOT documented in the README: add a '### subtract(a, b)' entry", and it also adds a clamp entry. Item 2: verifier Check 3 prints the exported functions ("expect at least add, subtract, multiply, clamp") and says FAIL if "any exported function, e.g. subtract or clamp, is not documented". Item 3: verifier Check 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi ([5,10,0] and others) and tests `e instanceof RangeError`. It FAILs if a call "throws something that is not a RangeError". All three items are handled.

avoids-must-not.why:
Criterion met: the briefs do neither thing on the must_not list.

Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function and fails if "any exported function, e.g. subtract or clamp, is not documented in README.md". A README that documents clamp but not subtract therefore fails.

Item 2: no PASS or FAIL condition is stricter than its expect line.
- Check 1 only needs an exported clamp function with correct limiting results.
- Check 2 only needs a RangeError. It doesn't check the error message.
- Check 3 needs "an entry that names it and describes what it does", not a particular layout.
- Check 4 only needs the tests to pass.

The stricter points (the grep for headings, entries under "## API", the message naming lo and hi, exit status 0) all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". The builder's "e.g." message and the style guidance are suggestions, not gates.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's probes, and the builder brief breaks the criterion. Step 2 tells the builder to test exactly these inputs and results: "clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100", "clamp(42, 0, 100) === 42" and "assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError)". The same inputs and results appear in the verifier's probes, as the Check 1 cases [-5,0,100,0], [140,0,100,100] and [42,0,100,42], and as the Check 2 case [5,10,0]. Writing its own tests is allowed, but these are the checker's own inputs with expected outputs. Step 4 also gives the builder `node -e "...Object.keys(m)..."` to check README coverage. That is nearly the same as the Check 3 probe command, and no expect line or the issue names it. So the builder is handed the checker's methods, not just the bar.
